title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 2nd District
area: South metro Twin Cities suburbs and exurbs, including Lakeville, Prior Lake, Burnsville, Eagan and Hastings.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Angie Craig (D) did not run for re-election here, running instead in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate (where she lost to Peggy Flanagan, 58.9%-39.5%). Matt Little, a former state senator, won the Democratic primary over four others. Eric Pratt, a state senator, won the Republican primary unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Matt Little

summary.text: Matt Little is the Democratic nominee for the open 2nd District seat. A Lakeville native and attorney, he served on the Lakeville City Council, as mayor of Lakeville and in the Minnesota Senate. According to his campaign website, he is running on Medicare for All, affordable childcare, tax breaks for everyday Americans and a tax on the ultrawealthy.

background.text: Born and raised in Lakeville, Minnesota; attended Parkview Elementary School and graduated from Rosemount High School, according to his campaign website. He now lives in New Market Township.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Minnesota, Morris in 2007 and a law degree from the University of Minnesota in 2014.
According to his campaign website, taught English abroad in Chile for a year before being elected to the Lakeville City Council in 2010.
Elected Mayor of Lakeville in 2012, while still in law school, and was unopposed for re-election in 2014, according to his campaign website.
Has owned a law firm since 2015 that, he says, represents seniors and people with disabilities in negligence and abuse cases against insurance companies.
Served in the Minnesota State Senate representing District 58 (Lakeville, Farmington and southern Dakota County) from 2017 to 2021, before losing re-election in 2020 to Zach Duckworth (R).
Describes himself as having authored or co-authored over 60 bipartisan bills as a state senator, including the Alec Smith Insulin Affordability Act, which passed in 2020.
Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary for Minnesota's 2nd District.

priorities.text: Says he is running to fight for people who work hard but 'still can't get ahead,' and for families struggling to afford groceries, child care, health care and assisted living.
Says he supports cutting red tape and eliminating wasteful spending, but opposes what he describes as cuts made by the current administration to life-saving programs.
Frames his campaign around defending democracy and the rule of law, and says he wants to work across the aisle with bipartisan experience.

positions.summary: Says he is fighting for families who cannot afford health care, and opposes federal cuts to vital public services.

record.text: Served as a Minnesota state senator representing District 58 from 2017 to 2021.
Voted no on HF 2125 (the Senate Republican majority's 2019 omnibus tax bill), which passed the Minnesota Senate 39-28 on 2019-04-30.

candidates.researchNotes: Matt Little has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions are drawn from Ballotpedia's summary of his campaign website's 'Key Issues' page rather than a direct fetch of that page. Only one recorded floor vote is documented here: unlike the Minnesota House, the Minnesota Senate does not publish a searchable online roll-call database, so individual votes had to be located in scanned Senate Journal PDFs bill-by-bill; within the research budget, other consequential 2017-2020 bills touching the guide's 15 issue categories (e.g. a 2019 universal-background-check gun proposal) were not found to have reached a full Senate floor vote during his term.

candidates.name: Eric Pratt
candidates.currentRole: Minnesota State Senator, District 54 (since 2023; previously District 55, 2013-2023)

summary.text: Eric Pratt is the Republican nominee for the open 2nd District seat. A Prior Lake native with a career in banking and finance, he began in public service on the Prior Lake-Savage school board and has served in the Minnesota Senate since 2013. His campaign website describes his priorities as affordability, safer communities and accountability.

background.text: Born and raised in Prior Lake, Minnesota, where he still lives; graduated from Prior Lake High School. His campaign website says his father worked in real estate and his mother taught in Shakopee for more than 25 years.
Earned a B.A. in economics from the University of Colorado, Boulder, where he played Division I football, and an M.B.A. in finance from the University of St. Thomas.

Worked in banking and finance, including as an analyst at ITT Consumer Finance and First Banks System, assistant vice president at FirstPlus Financial, senior group manager at Target, and senior vice president of risk management at U.S. Bank.
Began his public service on the Prior Lake-Savage school board.
Elected to the Minnesota Senate in 2012 (District 55, taking office in 2013); has represented District 54 since January 2023.

In the state Senate, chaired the Jobs and Economic Growth Finance and Policy Committee in 2019-2020 and 2021-2022; for 2025-2026 he is ranking minority member of the Finance Committee and sits on the Capital Investment Committee.
Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary for Minnesota's 2nd District.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife Tina have been married 34 years and raised two children, Cam and Sammi, in the district.

priorities.text: 'Restore economic stability and opportunity': says he will focus on lowering costs and supporting small businesses.
'Protect communities and keep families safe': supports law enforcement and first responders, and says laws should be enforced consistently, including at the border.
'Keep bad actors out of our wallets': says he will work to crack down on fraud and abuse of government programs.

positions.summary: Says laws should be enforced fairly and consistently 'from our neighborhoods to the U.S. Border.'
Says he supports law enforcement, first responders and policies that keep communities secure.

record.text: Has served in the Minnesota State Senate since 2013 (District 55, 2013-2023; District 54, 2023-present); currently ranking minority member of the Senate Finance Committee and a member of the Capital Investment and Jobs and Economic Growth Finance and Policy committees.
